c.tagline: The world's smallest state, home to the Pope and the greatest art on Earth.

taxi.fareNote: No taxis or ride-hail pick up inside the Vatican walls; use licensed white Rome taxis from the ranks at Piazza del Risorgimento or the edge of St. Peter's Square, or Rome's Free Now / Uber. Fixed fares apply from Rome's airports (about €55 from Fiumicino).

emergency.note: Within the enclave the Vatican Gendarmerie polices the state; for emergencies dial Rome's 112 (police) or 118 (ambulance), or the EU-wide 112.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Pickpockets work the crowds in St Peter's Square and museum queues; ignore unofficial 'skip-the-line' ticket touts on the approach streets.

hood_desc: The largest church in the world and the spiritual centre of Roman Catholicism, built over the tomb of St. Peter and topped by Michelangelo's dome; inside are Michelangelo's Pietà and Bernini's bronze baldachin, and you can climb the cupola for sweeping views over Rome.

Bernini's vast oval piazza, embraced by two sweeping colonnades of 284 columns crowned with saints and centred on an ancient Egyptian obelisk; the gathering place for papal audiences and the Sunday Angelus blessing.

A roughly 7-kilometre sequence of galleries holding one of the world's greatest art collections — the Raphael Rooms, the Gallery of Maps, Egyptian and classical antiquities — leading ultimately to the Sistine Chapel; queues are long, so book a timed ticket ahead.

The Sistine Chapel, with Michelangelo's ceiling and 'Last Judgment' and the site of papal conclaves, sits at the end of the museum route; beyond it stretch the manicured Vatican Gardens, which cover half the city-state and are seen only by guided tour or the open-top bus.

The atmospheric medieval quarter between the Vatican and Castel Sant'Angelo, threaded by grand Via della Conciliazione and narrow lanes of trattorias, guesthouses and souvenir shops; together with neighbouring Prati it is where most visitors actually stay and eat.

water.note: Tap and fountain water is safe and excellent, as throughout Rome.

transit.hours: Rome's Metro Line A runs about 5:30am-11:30pm (until 1:30am Fri-Sat); night buses cover the network afterwards. Everything within the Vatican itself is reached on foot.
transit.note: The only rail inside the walls is the ceremonial Vatican railway station, which has no scheduled passenger service.
transit.pay: Vatican City has no transit system of its own; you ride Rome's ATAC network. Buy a BIT ticket (€1.50/$1.60, valid 100 minutes) from tobacco shops or machines, or tap a contactless card at metro gates. Line A stops Ottaviano-San Pietro and Cipro sit just outside the walls, a short walk from St. Peter's and the Vatican Museums.

transit.m: Leonardo Express to Termini, then Metro A to Ottaviano (~50 min)
FL1 regional train to Roma San Pietro (~45 min)
Taxi (fixed €55 fare from FCO to central Rome)

tip.r: Service (servizio) or a cover charge (coperto) is often included; round up or leave a euro or two for good service.
